items.name: ologit cut-point covariance [correct Jacobian reference]
notes: statsmodels stores thresholds as [c1, log(c2-c1), log(c3-c2)]; the correct Jacobian to Stata's cut points is cut_k = theta[0] + sum_{j<=k} exp(theta[j]), so J[k,0]=1 for every k and J[k,j]=exp(theta[j]) for 1<=j<=k
with that Jacobian the FULL e(V) (incl. slope-cut and cut-cut cross terms) reproduces Stata to 1.01e-06, whereas westata's reported e(V) is off by 5.56e-11

westata's _to_cut_points builds J = eye(n_cut) with J[k,:k] = exp(theta[1:k+1]): row 0 is never given the theta[0] loading and the cumulative terms are shifted, so cut1's SE happens to survive while cut2 and cut3's SEs are wrong (they can even exceed cut3's point estimate)
the point estimates themselves are correct: the cut values are rebuilt by the same recursion

items.name: e(chi2) LR -> Wald switch under vce(robust)/vce(cluster)
items.command: logit/poisson/nbreg with vce(robust) and vce(cluster g)
notes: Stata switches e(chi2) from the LR statistic to a Wald statistic as soon as vce(robust)/vce(cluster) is requested (e(chi2type) goes 'LR' -> 'Wald'), and that Wald excludes the constant: recomputing b'V^-1 b on the slope block reproduces e(chi2) to 2.19e-16 for every one of the five commands, while including the constant is off by a factor of several.
westata now reproduces Stata's e(chi2) for all five commands to 3.59e-09 (before the repair it reported the LR statistic regardless of cov_type, a 37% gap for logit-cluster).

items.name: e(df_m) must exclude auxiliary parameters
notes: Stata's e(df_m) counts only the main equation's regressors beyond the constant; /lnalpha (nbreg/tnbreg) and cut1..cutk (ologit/oprobit) are reported separately through e(k_aux) and never enter df_m
westata's _DiscreteBase._stata_scalars sets df_m = len(params) - 1, which counts the auxiliary parameters: nbreg/tnbreg report df_m=3 vs Stata's 2 and ologit/oprobit report df_m=4 vs Stata's 2

consequence: e(p), the printed 'LR chi2(df)' label and any downstream df-based test are wrong for those four commands. CountBase._model_df gets this right for zip/zinb/ztp, so the bug is specific to the statsmodels-backed path
